newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bonds strode firmer in active Tuesday trade as a combination of offshore and local institutional buying, jobber short-covering and option-related demand pushed yields about 15 basis points lower on the day
Shortly after 1400 GMT, the key R150 was pegged at a 14.81 percent yield compared with 14.95 percent late on Monday.

The market initially ticked above the 15 percent level as jobbers sold stock in the wake of weakness on the U.S. Treasury bond market overnight, where the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose to 7.10 percent from around 7.05 percent previously.
But the initial bout of selling was met by local institutional demand which forced jobbers to cover their short positions.
Dealers said there was also good offshore demand for local stock as London-based players sought to hedge themselves for the newly announced Eurorand issues.

U.S. investment bank JP Morgan earlier announced the launch of a one billion rand 15-year zero coupon bond for the World Bank. It was followed by Hambros, which announced that Swedish Export Credit had set a two billion rand 20-year zero coupon bond.
Demand related to the options close-out on May was also cited as a reason for the market's gains on the day.
Dealers said local sentiment had been bolstered by a fall in the money market shortage to its lowest level in six months.
The Reserve Bank said the shortage fell to 6.743 billion rand on Monday -- its lowest level since September 25 last year when it was pegged at 6.989 billion rand.
But the drop in the shortage was largely a result of a mismatch in government flows, a Reserve Bank official said, and it was likely to "correct" over the next couple of days.

Despite the expected rise in the shortage on Wednesday, banks edged their deposit rates lower to between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered from 16.45 to 16.50 percent on Monday. The 90-day BA rate also eased to between 15.80 to 16.00 percent from 15.85 and 16.05 previously.
One trader felt there was scope for NCD rates to fall further in the short-term, given the improved liquidity in the market.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals cautioned however that suggestions that the decline in the shortage signalled an end to the recent liquidity squeeze were premature.
Stals also told Reuters that the reason for the decline in the shortage was a fall in notes and coins in circulation and an increase in gold and foreign exchange reserves.
Traders said that as Stals had pointed to technical factors as the reason for the fall, the market was now likely to be more cautious on the positive signals currently emanating from the short-end.
Technically, however, traders said the market looked good after moving back below the 14.98 percent earlier in the day.
One senior trader said that the break below signalled that yields could revisit the 14.50 level in the short-term -- an area last seen early in March.

The improved mood on the bond market spilled over into the currency market, although the rand held its gound in what some traders said had been a day characterised by good exporter and importer flows as well as offshore dollar selling.
The rand was last quoted at 4.4465/4485 against the dollar from 4.4460/4490 overnight having traded in a 4.4400 to 4.4470 range during the day.
Dealers said they expected more of the same on Wednesday, with the rand expected to range-trade between 4.44 and 4.45.

Against the crosses, the rand was trading at 28.3473/3889 yen from 28.2262/2677 on Monday, at 0.3846/3850 marks from 0.3831/3835 marks previously and at 7.2727/2820 against sterling from 7.2614/2707 overnight.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners were net buyers of 182.85 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after selling 115.27 million rand's worth on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were 3.15 billion rand from 5.5 billion rand previously.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
